source.title: Slicing Mutual Information Generalization Bounds for Neural Networks
source.authors: Kimia Nadjahi; Kristjan H. Greenewald; Rickard Brüel Gabrielsson; J. Solomon

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures generalization error and training/test risks under changes to random-subspace dimension, quantization, and a compressibility penalty, using a different intervention from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own generalization results for random-subspace dimension, quantization levels, and a regularization coefficient. Results cited from prior work are not extracted. Several neural-network results are available only as plots, so their values are recorded as figure only. None of the eight versions directly describes the random-slicing and compressibility interventions tested here.
record.test_reason: The study tests random-subspace compression, quantization and compressibility regularization, none of which measures V1–V8. Varying subspace dimension is not widening a network; compressibility is not magnitude-aware sharpness. Using Adam without an optimizer comparison does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive tighter, more tractable input-output mutual-information bounds using random slicing and approximate compressibility, and propose compressibility regularization. Their experiments demonstrate a trade-off: stronger compression can reduce the generalization gap while increasing predictive risk, although suitable settings retain satisfactory performance. They do not establish that tighter bounds generally imply lower test error.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains neural networks on random parameter subspaces or encourages approximate compressibility, then evaluates generalization errors and information-theoretic bounds; it does not test the listed interventions directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Random-subspace dimension d, regularization coefficient λ, and quantization levels L change reported generalization outcomes; the study also reports training/test risks changing with λ and d.

fits_no_version.finding: Slicing followed by quantization yields non-vacuous information-theoretic bounds for MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks, with retained test performance at suitable subspace dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-subspace training and quantization can enable computable generalization bounds while retaining useful image-classification performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger compressibility regularization lowers the generalization gap and bound, while stronger regularization and smaller subspaces raise training and test risks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Encouraging approximate compressibility can tighten generalization bounds and reduce the training–test loss gap while worsening predictive risk.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing quantization levels increases the generalization gap across the tested MNIST subspace dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More aggressive quantization reduces the generalization gap in the tested projected-weight networks.

fits_no_version.finding: For Gaussian-data logistic regression, smaller subspaces lower the generalization gap but increase test risk; the proposed bound follows gap changes across n and d.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting logistic regression to smaller random subspaces trades a smaller generalization gap for higher test risk.

record.problems: The paper notes that kNN-MI produced NaN values for d > 2, so those bounds are reported using MINE. Neural-network outcome values in the cited plots are not stated numerically in the text. Some experiments use estimates over a limited number of random subspaces or runs, as specified in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result rows were omitted. Prior-work results cited in the paper were excluded.

untested.parts: No comparison of fixed random-label fitting with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error; architecture widths remain fixed.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or comparison of tuning regimes.
No controlled batch-size comparison under fixed epochs or adapted training recipes.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measure, gap-ranking analysis or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based selection and removal of training examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 classification should be changed because no listed version is tested. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, rather than evidence that those effects are absent. No unrecorded result bearing on V1–V8 was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning or training recipes.
Large-batch versus small-batch training and epoch-budget adjustments.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: fully-connected NNs
rows.size_stated: D = 199 210 for MNIST; D = 656 810 for CIFAR-10; 2 fully-connected layers of width 200
rows.operation_detail: Train on random d-dimensional parameter subspaces and vary d; estimate generalization error.

conditions.value: different values of d; results in Figure 5

rows.note: The paper says it reports results for different d; plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: No claim version applies. Figure 5 concerns subspace training with MINE-estimated bounds; distinguish it from the projected-and-quantized MNIST experiment in Figure 3a. Generalization error means the training–population loss gap, not test error.

rows.subject: fully-connected NNs
rows.size_stated: D = 199 210 for MNIST; D = 656 810 for CIFAR-10; 2 fully-connected layers of width 200
rows.operation_detail: Train on random d-dimensional parameter subspaces and vary d; estimate generalization error.
rows.note: The text describes Figure 3 as illustrating non-vacuous bounds while maintaining test performance for adequate d; exact plotted errors are not stated.
rows.check: No claim version applies. Figure 3b evaluates slicing followed by quantization; include quantization in the operation and condition. Separate the generalization gap, bound, training error and test error if recording these outcomes.

rows.subject: 3-layer feedforward NN f
rows.size_stated: D = 1 794 000; first two layers each contain 1000 neurons and final layer has K = 10 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Add a penalty weighted by λ to encourage parameters to lie near a d-dimensional random subspace.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over 5 runs; shaded areas represent the 2.5% and 97.5% percentiles.
rows.note: The text states that higher λ lowers generalization error and tightens the bound, while train/test risks rise as λ increases and d decreases; numeric plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: No claim version applies. This combines several dimensions, regularization strengths and measures. Separate the gap, bound, training/test risks and accuracies. The text establishes directional changes despite unavailable exact plot values.

rows.subject: feedforward neural network with 2 fully-connected layers of width 200
rows.operation_detail: Vary the number of quantization levels L for quantized projected weights.
rows.note: The text states that generalization error increases with increasing L for all tested dimensions; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: No claim version applies. Increasing quantization levels increases the reported generalization gap, not necessarily held-out error. The directional result is explicit in the text, although exact values are unavailable.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Train on random d-dimensional subspaces and vary d; estimate generalization error and test risk.
rows.note: The text states that lower d gives lower generalization error and bound but higher test risk; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: No claim version applies. Separate generalization gap and test risk: decreasing d lowers the former but raises the latter. Record the sample-count condition rather than pooling all n.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Train on random d-dimensional subspaces and vary sample count n and d; compare generalization error with a bound.
rows.note: The authors say the bound holds and accurately reflects generalization error as a function of n and d; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: No claim version applies. This overlaps R5's Figure 2 generalization-gap results. Consolidate duplicate observations; keep evaluation of the proposed bound separate from model outcomes.
